title: Knots on a Torus: A Model of the Elementary Particles
note: Independent prior art for a knot-to-particle dictionary. Avrin models the four basic fermions as flattened Moebius strips whose boundaries are the unknot (half-twist n = -1, +1: neutron or neutrino, and proton) and the trefoil (n = -3: electron; n = +3: a charge +2e partner required by symmetry). Charge is read off the corners ('quirks', +2e/3 and -e/3) and is linear in twist; bosons are fermion-antifermion composites (W- = electron + antineutrino); three generations come from an icosahedral SU(3) scaffold. The paper uses no quarks, gluons or Higgs and does not use hyperbolic volume. QOU's Hecke / Markov-trace and volume content is not taken from it.
